items.title: If you are building AI for finance, get out while you can
items.description: LLMs are good with probabilistic logic (words), but not as good with deterministic logic (numbers). As oppose to what everybody thought 3 years ago, LLMs are not very good with finance. Makes sense when you think about it as AI in 2025 still rely heavily on language transformers, and transformers are more or less probability calculators. Ai agents in accounting firms are way less effective than Ai agents in law firms for example. 1 wrong word in the bylaws can break your entire company. Accounting is more precise, it tolerates less mistakes, and the rules that govern it are much less option to intrepretation. In accounting, the rules are more grounded. Not in precedent but in a generally accepted specific rulebook. Gross profits mean the same in the US as it does in Bangladesh, and it will mean the same 100 years in the future. items.title: Show HN: Searching for optimal strategies in a puzzle game with chance (Drop7)
items.description: Sixteen years ago, I wrote a Java program which tried to pick the ideal move in a puzzle game called Drop7. On each turn, the player only has seven choices for their next move, but there is also an element of chance which turns this simple game into a surprisingly difficult problem involving search, hidden information, long-term planning, and chance. I renewed my investigation this weekend, into whether there is an autonomous strategy that averages more than one million points per game. An experienced human player can score a million points with long-term strategic thinking, but the best automated strategies I could come up with are currently averaging around 300k-400k points. One of the easiest ways to contribute to advancing this research is to compete on the global leaderboard and submit your human strategy - https://drop7.dev/compete . This project has also been an enlightening experiment into using agents as research collaborators and evidence collectors. Repository: https://githu
items.title_vi: Show HN: Tìm kiếm chiến lược tối ưu trong game giải đố mang tính may rủi (Drop7)
items.title_en: Show HN: Searching for optimal strategies in a puzzle game with chance (Drop7)
items.summary_vi: Mười sáu năm trước, tôi đã viết một chương trình Java nhằm cố gắng chọn nước đi lý tưởng trong một trò chơi giải đố có tên Drop7. Ở mỗi lượt, người chơi chỉ có bảy lựa chọn cho bước đi tiếp theo của mình, nhưng cũng có yếu tố may rủi biến trò chơi đơn giản này thành một bài toán khó đến bất ngờ liên quan đến tìm kiếm, ẩn thông tin, lập kế hoạch dài hạn và may rủi. Tôi đã gia hạn cuộc điều tra của mình vào cuối tuần này để xem liệu có chiến lược tự trị nào đạt trung bình hơn một triệu điểm mỗi trò chơi hay không. Một người chơi có kinh nghiệm có thể ghi được một triệu điểm nhờ tư duy chiến lược dài hạn, nhưng các chiến lược tự động tốt nhất mà tôi có thể nghĩ ra hiện đạt trung bình khoảng 300k-400k điểm. items.summary_en: Sixteen years ago, I wrote a Java program which tried to pick the ideal move in a puzzle game called Drop7. On each turn, the player only has seven choices for their next move, but there is also an element of chance which turns this simple game into a surprisingly difficult problem involving search, hidden information, long-term planning, and chance. I renewed my investigation this weekend, into whether there is an autonomous strategy that averages more than one million points per game. An experienced human player can score a million points with long-term strategic thinking, but the best automated strategies I could come up with are currently averaging around 300k-400k points.
